animated_svg.summary: SVG animation techniques for a WebKit-rendered desktop app. Three tiers: CSS @keyframes (declarative ambient), Web Animations API (imperative interactive), SMIL (path morphing). GPU-composited properties only: transform, opacity, filter(drop-shadow). Stroke-dashoffset for line-drawing and progress indicators. SVG symbol + currentColor + CSS custom properties for theme-aware animated icons. Use will-change sparingly. Honor prefers-reduced-motion.
recommendations: CSS @keyframes for loading spinners, ambient backgrounds, dash-offset progress
WAAPI element.animate() for icon state transitions (play/pause, expand/collapse)
CSS filter: drop-shadow() for hover/active glow (GPU-composited)
CSS custom properties on SVG symbols for resolution-independent themed icons
Avoid: SVG filter primitives on animated elements (CPU-bound), width/height animations (triggers layout), will-change in static CSS (memory bloat)

webkit_features.summary: Modern CSS/HTML/JS features shipping in Safari 26.x (2025-2026) that a pywebview/WKWebView desktop app can exploit. Critical new features: @layer cascade layers, View Transitions API (single-document), popover API + commandfor, <dialog>, field-sizing: content, :has() parent selector, content-visibility: auto, scrollend event, scroll-driven animations (threaded in 26.4). pywebview WKWebView provides full Safari feature parity. Service Workers NOT available (requires HTTPS origin).
p0_immediate: content-visibility: auto on chat history and scrollable lists (one CSS line, large performance win)
@layer cascade layers in CSS (eliminates specificity bugs)
p1_medium: <dialog> for modals/confirmations (built-in focus trap, backdrop, ESC)
popover + commandfor for dropdowns and tooltips (declarative, no z-index wars)
field-sizing: content for chat input (auto-growing without JS)
:has() for state-driven styling (fewer JS state mirrors)
p2_later: View Transitions for layout-mode switches (smooth Operator→Review→System)
Threaded scroll-driven animations for 'new content' indicators

nintendo_ui_ux.summary: Nintendo does not publish public UI/UX guidelines. Best primary source: CEDEC 2018 presentation on Switch OS design. Core philosophy: radical minimalism (<200KB home menu), game-first (NES inspiration — boot directly to game), near-zero animation budget, no background music, flat navigation (one level deep), no ads in system UI, family-safe by default. Switch 2 adds 'Basic Dark' theme but maintains same flat architecture. Key transferable principles: minimize startup resources, avoid deep menu nesting, keep transitions under 200ms, offer dark/light only (no theme store), ensure keyboard navigability, make app reopen near-instant.
transferable_principles: Minimize startup resource usage; keep boot time under 1 second
Flat navigation — surface core actions directly, avoid deep nesting
No background music by default — audio as functional feedback only
Dark/Light only — no theme system complexity
All UI keyboard-navigable with generous click targets
Session restore near-instant on app reopen
No promotional content in app chrome
Destructive actions: single undo, not confirmation dialog
Subtle click sounds on button press; optional haptic feedback
primary_sources: CEDEC 2018 Nintendo Switch OS Development Session (via Nintendo Life)

accessibility.summary: Comprehensive accessibility audit for a pywebview/WKWebView desktop app. Current codebase: strong ARIA coverage (30+ aria-labels, live regions, landmark roles, proper focus-visible). Key gaps: missing skip link, no prefers-color-scheme: light, no prefers-contrast support, no focus trapping in modal dialog, missing KeyboardEvent handlers for arrow-key navigation in tabs, missing keyboard shortcuts (Cmd+Enter, Cmd+K). WebKit on macOS fully supports ARIA → NSAccessibility mapping for VoiceOver. Testing tools: axe-core injection, macOS Accessibility Inspector, Lighthouse (via --server-only mode).
current_strengths: aria-live='polite' on chat transcript, status chips, notifications
aria-selected on tabs and mode buttons
Proper landmark roles (navigation, main, complementary, contentinfo, dialog, region)
gaps: Missing skip link for bypass blocks (WCAG 2.4.1 Level A)
Focus trapping in modal dialog missing (declared aria-modal without JS)
No arrow-key navigation in tab panels (WAI-ARIA APG Tabs Pattern)
AccentColor system keyword not used (hardcoded blue)
No automated accessibility testing in CI pipeline

procedural_background_music.summary: Feasibility assessment for procedurally generated ambient background music in a pywebview desktop app. Technical feasibility: HIGH — Web Audio API + Tone.js are production-ready. MVP: 4-layer ambient drone (sub-bass, mid pad, high shimmer, gentle pulse) via pure synthesis, ~100-200 lines of JS. CPU budget: 2-5%. Parameter mapping: agent activity → note density/filter openness; tool execution → rhythmic pulse layer; error state → subtle harmonic shift. Default to OFF, require user opt-in. Zero copyright risk with pure synthesis. Key design principle: volume should be barely perceptible ('you don't notice it until it's gone').

recommended_stack.transport: WebSocket from Python backend pushes audio_state → JS AudioEngine.update()

parameter_mapping.agent_idle: reduce note density, lower filter cutoff, slower LFO
parameter_mapping.agent_thinking: slightly brighter filter, subtle harmonic motion
parameter_mapping.error: subtle dissonance — detune oscillators, minor shift

user_controls: style selector (ambient drone / lo-fi pulse / nature blend)
procedural_background_music.accessibility: default OFF, opt-in only, volume very low, no abrupt changes, prefer-no-audio-reactivity media query analogue
primary_sources: Paul Weir GDC talks (No Man's Sky)
